hpi: {{patient_name}} is an HIV-positive woman with unknown CD4 count who presents with cough, dyspnea, and hypoxemia. She has concurrent candida vulvovaginitis from poorly controlled HIV. CD4 is likely <200 given the presentation with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia — the most common respiratory infection in HIV patients not on prophylaxis. CXR shows classic diffuse bilateral perihilar interstitial infiltrates. Elevated LDH supports the diagnosis (though not specific). ABG shows hypoxemia with PaO2 >70, so oral TMP-SMX is first-line. Screen for TB, bacterial pneumonia, and other OIs. Start ART based on viral load and CD4. Admit to inpatient/ICU. PCP prophylaxis indicated when CD4 <200.
